deep-teal.purpose: Links, the CV button, award badges, current nav item, focus (light)

deep-teal-night.purpose: The same jobs in the dark theme

teal-tint.purpose: Hover fill of buttons, text selection, targeted paper label (light)

display.purpose: your name in the header, nowhere else.

lead.purpose: the research question. The second thing a visitor reads.

subtitle.purpose: the position line under your name. The same size, roman 500 in Ink, sets your name in the top bar.

title.purpose: every title of a work: papers, theses and research topics; also the Quick facts heading. On phones (760px and below) it steps to 1.125rem, all titles together.

body.purpose: the bio, details and all running text, at most 38em wide. Paragraphs use `text-wrap: pretty`, so no word sits alone on a last line.

small.purpose: secondary text: authors, the venue line, the organisation line under each entry (in Ink), details, abstracts, research-topic text, the link row, navigation and the CV button. Links and controls in it use 500.

label.purpose: dates on the spine, the figure caption and the footer small print at 400; paper labels (C5), year rules and Quick facts terms at 600 with 0.02em tracking.

motion.name: figure-draw
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: the first time the research figure scrolls into view, the staircase draws itself through the Pareto front. The points, A, B and the question are there from the start.

motion.name: ticker
motion.purpose: The rotating latest-news line; pauses on hover, keyboard focus, the Pause button, or a tap on an arrow (phones).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animation and transitions off; the ticker never advances; the figure's staircase is simply drawn.

breakpoints.name: facts-below
breakpoints.purpose: Quick facts move under the bio; the photo stops hanging into the margin.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: The date column folds away and dates sit above entries on one line; the nav wraps to its own row; the research figure stacks above the topics; the header links form a two-by-two grid.

narrative.overview:
The site is a researcher's record, set quietly. The research question, the papers and their venues carry the page; the design stays out of the way and lets the evidence be read. It answers to two readers at once: a hiring committee member skimming for a few minutes, and a reader who checks every claim. Both are served by the same thing: a clear spine, honest labels, and nothing that competes with the content.

Restraint is the method, not the absence of one. Colour is rare and always means something: one accent, Deep Teal, with a short fixed list of jobs. Type does the ranking: the Newsreader serif for your name, the research question, section and paper titles; Hanken Grotesk for everything you read through. There is one authored moment of motion, the research figure drawing its Pareto front, plus the news ticker. Components are precise and quiet: hairline outlines, underlined links, no shadows, nothing that asks for attention it hasn't earned.

Confirmed rejections: the indigo, glow-lit "AI product" look the site started with; decorative colour on labels, icons and dividers; cards used as page structure.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, Deep Teal, kept to five jobs
A near-white page with Mint Wash bands; a deep Petrol Night in dark mode, composed rather than inverted
Serif for names, titles and the question; sans for reading and labels
A date and label column, the spine, running down every list
Flat: tonal bands and 1px hairlines, never shadows
Every link underlined; every text colour at 4.5:1 or more in both themes

rules.name: The Rare Teal Rule
rules.body: Deep Teal does five jobs only: links, the CV button, award badges, the current section in the top bar, focus and selection. Labels, years, icons, dots and dividers stay Ink or Muted Slate.

rules.name: The Underline Rule
rules.body: Every link is underlined, and nothing else is. The icon link rows (Email, CV, profiles) keep Ink text with a faint Ink underline, so the CV button stays the only accent on the first screen. The only exceptions are links that look like controls: the name and section links in the top bar, the CV button, and the paper labels (permalinks that tint on hover). Colour never carries meaning on its own.

rules.name: The Spine Rule
rules.body: Dates and paper labels sit in the left column with tabular figures, right-aligned; content sits in the text column to its right. A date range stacks its start over its end, so every range in the column has the same shape; on phones the date sits above its entry on one line.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: Every font size is one of the eight `--text-*` tokens at the top of `static/style.css` (display, headline, lead, subtitle, title, body, small, label). A new element takes an existing role; it never gets a size of its own.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and on hover. Depth comes from tone and hairlines; a hover changes the outline or a tint, never a shadow.

rules.name: The One Moment Rule
rules.body: One authored animation (the research figure) plus the news ticker. Nothing else moves; reduced motion turns everything off.

dos: Do keep Deep Teal to its five jobs (The Rare Teal Rule).
Do underline every link (The Underline Rule).
Do keep every text colour at 4.5:1 or more against page, band and card, in both themes; check new colours with a contrast tool before shipping.
Do put dates and labels on the spine, right-aligned, with tabular figures.
Do add new lists as rows on the spine, like Education and Teaching.
Do drive new features from fields in `content/` and document them in the README; updating the site never means editing templates.
Do change colours in all three token blocks and the two `theme-color` tags together.
Do respect reduced motion: anything that moves must stop under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't add glows, radial gradients or decorative backgrounds; the site deliberately left that look behind.
Don't use the accent on labels, years, icons, dots, dividers or other decoration.
Don't add fonts, icon fonts, CDNs, analytics or any other third-party request.
Don't use cards as page structure or for lists.
Don't add motion beyond the research figure and the news ticker.
Don't put the email address in plain text anywhere in the source.
